long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Sunday 20th September - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.




Where: Founders Heritage Park, (St Peters Church) 87 Atawhai Dr, The Wood, Nelson. 7010 NEW ZEALAND
When: Sunday 20th Sept 2026
10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm

Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.

Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. During her research, she interviewed leaders from all over the world — from Fortune 100 companies, non-profits, public sector entities, and more — and asked one question: what is the future of leadership?

Remarkably, their answers pointed to one thing: we need braver leaders.




We need more courage.




The most significant finding from Brené’s latest research, and the foundation of Dare to Lead™, is that courage is a collection of four skill sets that are teachable, measurable, and observable.

long_description:
Overview

Explore the connections between astrology, emotions and the body, and discover a deeper perspective on wellbeing beyond treating symptoms.

Heal the Cause, Not the Symptom
An Evening on Astrology, Emotion, and Where Disease Really Begins



Have you ever noticed how the body keeps trying to tell us something, and we just reach for a pill or a cream instead of listening?

After having worked one-on-one hundreds of people with many of which having physical issues. I have yet to find someone who's physical issue is not related to an emotional cause or imbalance in their lifestyle and their nature. Skin issues often relating people getting under your skin and not expressing what's harbouring inside. Tension in one's legs which often stays for lack of boundaries and stability (no foundation to stand on), often Anger that shows up as inflammation. Fear that locks into the gut or the joints. Studying astrology and ancient teachings has made this even clearer, because these traditions map exactly how specific planets and signs govern specific parts of the body, and what happens when we live out of step with our own nature and purpose.

That's really what disease is. Dis-ease. Being out of ease, carrying stress the body hasn't found a way to release.

Join us at Bhakti Lounge for an evening where we trace these connections directly: which planets and signs govern which parts of the body, why illness tends to land exactly where it does, and how to work with the root emotional cause instead of just managing symptoms with pills and creams.

Event start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.
A plant-based dinner & dessert follows the event - all included in your ticket!




Meet your host Gopi:

Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity and overcome challenges on their path through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counselling.

Wellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Critical minerals, material solutions (Wellington)
long_description:
Overview

The world wants minerals, but scientists around Aotearoa are working on what we could make instead.

The MacDiarmid Institute is a network of leading researchers from around the country united in a common goal: to create and explore innovative, sustainable materials that will improve the lives of people in Aotearoa New Zealand and around the word. This talk will focus on critical minerals - raw materials that are essential to many existing and future technologies and have been making headlines in recent times due to increasing supply chain vulnerabilities. In this talk we will present materials science solutions that are being developed and utilised right now, in Aotearoa New Zealand, to recycle, replace or reduce our need for critical minerals.

Speakers:
Professor Chris Bumby, Principal Investigator with the MacDiarmid Institute and Chief Scientist at Paihau - Robinson Research Institute

Professor Nicola Gaston, Principal Investigator and Director at the MacDiarmid Institute and Professor in Physics at the University of Auckland

Venue:
Lecture Theatre 2 (RHLT2), Rutheford House, 23 Lambton Quay/33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington

One free evening. A mortgage adviser, a lawyer, a real estate agent and a building inspector answer every first home question you have.

Thinking about buying your first home? Start here.

Buying your first home can feel overwhelming. There are deposits and pre-approvals and LVRs and a pile of jargon you've never heard before and underneath it all, the question that actually keeps you up: can I even get approved?

This evening is designed to answer that. No sales pitch, no pressure, no jargon left unexplained. Just a clear, honest walk through what it actually takes to buy your first home in Nelson, from the people who do this every day.

What we'll cover

Budgeting and deposits how much you actually need, and where it can come from
Pre-approval what lenders look at, and how to put yourself in the strongest position
The First Home Loan scheme who qualifies and how it works
Finding the right place what to look for, and what the current Nelson market is doing
Making an offer conditional vs unconditional, and where people get caught out
The legal side sale and purchase agreements, LIM reports, title, settlement
Builders' reports what a building inspection covers, and the red flags worth walking away from
And beyond what happens after you get the keys

Who you'll hear from

We've brought together the full team you'd normally have to chase down one at a time:

A Mike Pero mortgage adviser, on finance and pre-approval
A real estate agent, on searching, negotiating and the local market
A property lawyer, on contracts, conditions and settlement

There'll be time for questions, and you're welcome to stay afterwards for a one-on-one chat.

Who it's for

Anyone thinking about their first home whether you're planning to buy in the next few months or just starting to wonder if it's even possible. Bring your partner, bring a friend, bring your parents. Come with questions.

🎟️ Free to attend registration essential, seating is limited

After their rate rebates are cut, they form an independent micro-nation, appoint a queen, and go viral!
